original_question: Does there exist a maximal curve X over a finite field F_{q^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3, whose Frobenius linear series has second generic D-order epsilon_2 = 2, and which has an F_{q^2}-rational point P such that the second (D,P)-order satisfies j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1))?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting case (C) in the Introduction: the third of the three open cases asked to occur for maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3. In this paper, that question is later answered affirmatively by Theorem 4.1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical content of case (C) from the paper: an F_{q^2}-maximal curve with Frobenius dimension 3, second generic D-order epsilon_2 = 2, and an F_{q^2}-rational point P with j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1)). It also keeps the scope correctly at an existence question rather than broadening it into a classification problem.
missing_details: q should be quantified explicitly as a prime power; the paper's question is existential in q.
X should be specified as a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible curve over F_{q^2}.
"Maximal over F_{q^2}" should be made explicit as #X(F_{q^2}) = q^2 + 1 + 2gq, where g is the genus of X.
The Frobenius linear series D should be defined explicitly as D = |(q + 1)P_0| for an F_{q^2}-rational point P_0 on X.
"Frobenius dimension 3" should be spelled out as dim(D) = 3.
The generic D-order sequence should be introduced, namely 0 = epsilon_0 < epsilon_1 = 1 < epsilon_2 < epsilon_3 = q.
The pointwise (D,P)-orders should be introduced, namely 0 = j_0(P) < j_1(P) = 1 < j_2(P) < j_3(P) = q + 1 for P in X(F_{q^2}).
To be fully stand-alone, the question should distinguish the point P_0 used to define D from the point P at which j_2(P) is prescribed.
It should be explicit that the existence of the special rational point P is part of the claim in addition to the condition epsilon_2 = 2.
refined_question: Does there exist a prime power q and a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible F_{q^2}-maximal curve X such that, for an F_{q^2}-rational point P_0 on X and the associated Frobenius linear series D := |(q + 1)P_0|, one has dim(D) = 3, the generic D-order sequence 0 = epsilon_0 < epsilon_1 = 1 < epsilon_2 < epsilon_3 = q satisfies epsilon_2 = 2, and there exists a point P in X(F_{q^2}) whose (D,P)-orders 0 = j_0(P) < j_1(P) = 1 < j_2(P) < j_3(P) = q + 1 satisfy j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1))?
justification: The paper's Introduction first recalls the known restrictions on epsilon_2 and on the possible values of j_2(P) for F_{q^2}-rational points of maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3, and then lists three open cases (A), (B), and (C). Your draft matches case (C) exactly. The nearby context shows that the relevant linear series is the Frobenius linear series D = |(q + 1)P_0| and that epsilon_2 and j_2(P) are, respectively, its second generic order and second pointwise order. Theorem 4.1 then gives an explicit affirmative example over F_49: the function field defined by z^16 = t(t + 1)^6 has Frobenius dimension 3, D-order sequence (0, 1, 2, 7), and an F_49-rational place P with j_2(P) = 3 = 8 - floor((2/3) * 8), which is precisely case (C).
